turns.prompt_text: I've got some cronjobs on my mac air, I would like to delete them
turns.response_html:
Managing cron jobs on macOS is straightforward using the Terminal. Since you are using a Mac, you’ll likely be interacting with the crontab (cron table) file associated with your user account.

Step 1: View Your Current Cron Jobs

Before deleting anything, it is a good idea to see exactly what is running. Open your terminal and run:

crontab -l

Step 2: Delete All Cron Jobs

If you want to wipe the entire list of cron jobs for your user account at once, use the following command:

crontab -r

Note: This command is "silent" and will not ask for confirmation. It immediately removes all entries in your current user's crontab.

Step 3: Delete Specific Cron Jobs

If you only want to remove one or two specific lines but keep the rest, you need to enter the interactive editor:

  1. Type crontab -e in your terminal.
  2. This usually opens the file in Vim by default.
  3. Use the arrow keys to navigate to the line you want to delete.
  4. Press dd on your keyboard to delete the line.
  5. To save and exit, type :wq and press Enter.

A Note on macOS "Launch Agents"

Apple has technically deprecated cron in favor of launchd. If you run crontab -l and see nothing, but a task is still running automatically, it might be managed as a Launch Agent.

To check for those, you can look in these directories:

  • ~/Library/LaunchAgents (User-specific tasks)
  • /Library/LaunchAgents (System-wide tasks)

If you find a .plist file there corresponding to the job you want to stop, you can remove it using:

launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.job.plist
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.job.plist

Would you like to look into how to convert any of those old cron jobs into modern Launch Agents instead?
